🫧You don’t have to clean every window to clean your windows. 

When it’s just my front door windows or a small area, I don’t mix up a big batch and feel like I have to tackle the whole house — I mix a small batch just for that one spot.

DIY Small Batch Window Cleaner:
•6 cups warm water
•1 tablespoon All-Purpose Cleaning Soap or dish soap
•1 tablespoon rubbing alcohol 
Mix in a bowl, dip your cloth, rinse it often as you go, and buff dry with a soft, clean cloth.
Save this one for the next time you’ve got one window or one door that needs a quick clean — no pressure to do the whole house.

I always dust top to bottom and left to right - everything falls down ensuring I don’t miss anything. AND since I dust on Tuesdays, nothing gets too dusty and it keeps the task around 10-15 minutes for a quick dusting.

I clean bathrooms in the same order every time:
spray surfaces
let sit
wipe sink & counters
clean tub & shower
clean toilet top to bottom

Cleaning bathrooms in this order ensures that you’re not cross-contaminating and everything is getting thoroughly clean.

Your home might not need more of your time. It might need fewer of your decisions.

Think about how many things you decide over and over again:
What’s for dinner? 
When should I do laundry? 
When am I cleaning this? 
Where does this go? 
Who’s responsible for that? 
What am I forgetting?
Did they take the trash out?

Those little open decisions add up and they can make home feel much harder to manage than it needs to.

That’s why I created Making Home Easier, a brand-new 9-day live experience starting September 1.

We’re going to sit down together and figure out what’s taking up space in your head, make some decisions, create simple rhythms and defaults, and give your home less to ask of you.
